# Getting started on the cluster

## What a cluster is {#sec-cluster}

### Mental model

MedicineBow is a few hundred ordinary Linux servers ("nodes") wired together, all mounting the same
shared filesystems, all managed by a scheduler ([Slurm](https://slurm.schedmd.com/)) that decides
whose job runs where and when.

### Login nodes vs. compute nodes

There are two kinds of machines:

1. **Login nodes** (`mblog1`, `mblog2`) are the front door. When you `ssh` in or open a
terminal in the web portal, you land here. They are shared by everyone at once — dozens of
people editing files, submitting jobs, and moving data. Use them for lightweight work:
editing scripts, managing files, compiling small things, submitting and checking jobs.

2. **Compute nodes** are where computation happens. You never SSH to them directly; you ask
the scheduler for one (or many), and it gives you exclusive, dedicated access for a
bounded time. The default `mb` nodes have **96 CPU cores and ~1 TB of RAM each**, and the
GPU nodes carry up to **8 NVIDIA H100s**.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-nodes
%%| fig-cap: "You reach a shared login node from your laptop; the scheduler runs your jobs on dedicated compute nodes. All nodes see the same filesystems."
flowchart LR
    U["Your laptop"] -->|"ssh / web portal"| L
    subgraph MB ["MedicineBow"]
        L["Login nodes<br/>mblog1 / mblog2<br/>shared, lightweight only"]
        S{{"Slurm scheduler"}}
        L -->|"sbatch / salloc"| S
        S --> C1["Compute node"]
        S --> C2["Compute node"]
        S --> C3["GPU node"]
    end
    FS[("Shared filesystems<br/>home, project, scratch")]
    L --- FS
    C1 --- FS
    C2 --- FS
    C3 --- FS
    style MB fill:#f3eefb,stroke:#7a4fb5,color:#3a2a5a
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Don't compute on login nodes
A big job on `mblog1`/`mblog2` slows the machine for everyone logging in. ARCC monitors this and
kills runaway login-node processes (and emails you).
:::

## Getting access {#sec-account}

### Requesting a new project

1. Email **Josh Day** (<josh@rallypoint1.com>) or **Virginia Iglesias**
   (<virginia@innosphere.org>) with the desired:

   a. Project name (`cowy-<name>`; its directory will be `/project/cowy-<name>`)
   b. Project PI
   c. CPU hours requested
   d. GPU hours requested
   e. Storage needed beyond the 5 TB default, if any

   ASCEND uses a shared `/project/cowy` space for data sharing between projects, which ARCC
   will add you to automatically when your `cowy-<name>` project is approved.

2. PI fills out [new project request](https://uwyo.teamdynamix.com/TDClient/1940/Portal/Requests/Service/55398/New-Project-Request/Request).

### Adding users to a project

As an "Attachment" in the new project form, the PI provides details for each user to be added to the project:

1. First and last name
2. Email address
3. Institution
4. Phone number
5. Whether they are a foreign national under the ITAR/EAR definitions.

Alternatively, the PI can request users by contacting <arcc-help@uwyo.edu> with the project name and
above info for each user.

### UW accounts vs. ARCC-Only accounts

ASCEND spans UW, CSU, CU Boulder, Mines, NCAR, and NEON, so this distinction affects
collaborators:

| | Full UW account | ARCC-Only account |
|---|---|---|
| Who | UW-affiliated people | External collaborators without a UW identity |
| HPC (MedicineBow) | ✅ | ✅ |
| GitLab | ✅ | ✅ |
| **Globus data transfer** | ✅ | ❌ **cannot use Globus** |
| Other UW services | ✅ | ❌ |

::: {.callout-warning}
## ARCC-Only accounts and Globus
External collaborators on ARCC-Only accounts **cannot use Globus**, the recommended way to
move large datasets (@sec-moving-data). They'll need a *guest collection* set up for them,
or a UW person to broker transfers. Plan for this early if your data lives at CSU, NCAR, etc.
:::
